title: WSJF judgment
description: The judgment one wsjf-scorer session writes in the wsjf-scoring workflow: the candidate <workDir>/judgments/<level>/candidates/<key>.json, which jsonartifact.py validates against EpicJudgment or TaskJudgment here and publishes as judgments/<level>/<key>.json. `depscore.py record` (scoring.record) then writes the judged values to the beads; a value off the rubric's scale is rejected there. Only judged inputs belong here: RR-OE, reaches, cost of delay and WSJF are computed afterwards by `skills/wsjf/scripts/wsjf.py`, and a judgment never states them. Every item the session was given appears exactly once, in `scores` or in `unscored`.

EpicJudgment.description: One Epic's judgment, under the agent-teams-workforce:wsjf rubric at Epic level.

TaskJudgment.description: The sizes of one Epic's Tasks (or of one Task with no Epic), under the agent-teams-workforce:wsjf rubric at Task level. Value, time criticality and their confidence are inherited from the Epic by arithmetic and are not judged here.

EpicScore.description: The judged inputs of one Epic. The four size fields are given only when the judge input's `sizedFromTasks` is false; an Epic whose elaboration is done takes its size from its Tasks.

userBusinessValue.description: A rung of the rubric's User-Business Value scale, judged from the Epic's PRD.

timeCriticality.description: A rung of the rubric's Time Criticality scale, judged from the Epic's PRD.

confidence.description: The value confidence, an integer percent covering UBV and TC only.

rationale.description: One to three sentences per judged dimension, citing the PRD; `jobSize` names the reference jobs it was compared with and the factors that placed it, and is given only when the size was judged.

assumptions.description: One entry per assumption that could move a judged value.

TaskScore.description: The judged size of one Task. A Task above 13 should have been split: its rationale says so, and the size judged is recorded, never reduced to 13.

rationale.description: One line on the size: the reference jobs it was compared with.

assumptions.description: One entry per assumption that could move the size.

JobSize.description: The size estimate on the rubric's Fibonacci scale (`wsjf.py scales --level epic|task`): the relative amount of work to deliver the outcome.

SizeLow.description: The low end of the plausible range; the estimate lies inside the range.

SizeHigh.description: The high end of the plausible range.

SizeConfidence.description: The size confidence, an integer percent covering the size estimate alone.

Unscored.description: An item the session could not judge.

reason.description: The concrete missing input, for example that the matrix names no PRD for the Epic.
